messages:
Jonas Weber: trying to sanity check: which prompt sets / offline benchmarks are actually correlating w/ shadow signals so far? before we bake anything into rollout gates

Selene Huang: tl;dr: MT-Bench / AlpacaEval-ish correlate directionally w/ preference, but the variance is big once you add prod constraints (formatting, tool calls). the strongest correlation we’ve seen is *format adherence* prompts (JSON schema, function args) vs shadow “parse_success” + judge “followed_instructions”

Sana Farid: +1. when we slice by route type, correlation changes. support-chat routes: preference signals line up w/ our internal “helpfulness” set. tool routes: preference is noisy but “valid tool call” is very predictive. the whole “overall model score” from generic benchmarks is not stable enough to gate canaries

Olivia Grant: also note judge itself is a source of noise. if we change rubric/prompt, the correlation story changes. right now the most reliable regression detector from shadow runs is:
- output format/structure checks (deterministic)
- safety policy outcome deltas (deterministic-ish)
- latency/cost deltas (deterministic)
judge preference is useful but i’d be careful making it a hard stop for GA

Jin Woo Park: from metrics side: if we do “prompt set name” as a dimension, cardinality risk. we can have like 3-5 fixed buckets, otherwise it’ll explode. (see ENG-2435)

Logan Wright: +1. we can aggregate by `judge_profile` (small allowlist) and `route_id` and keep prompt-set details out of tags (store in events only / sampled). anything else will get dropped by guardrails

Jonas Weber: makes sense. what are the candidates for “small allowlist” prompt sets?

Selene Huang: proposal: ship minimal judge rubric first (1 profile) that’s broadly applicable + route-agnostic:
1) preference (A vs B) w/ “which is better for user”
2) instruction following (binary-ish)
3) format adherence (binary) — BUT only when route says it expects structured output
4) refusal/safety alignment (binary-ish) — mostly rely on policy engine outcome

Selene Huang: and then later add opt-in profiles per route class (tool calling, RAG, summarization) + customer-specific rubrics in private beta

Marissa Cole: product POV: i’d really like something we can explain simply in Console for beta. “Shadow win-rate” + “format success rate” + “safety outcomes” + “latency/cost deltas” is understandable. if we start w/ 6 different prompt sets + per-task rubrics it’ll be a mess

Sana Farid: agree. also for gating: we should recommend customers gate on format + safety + latency first. judge win-rate can be “warn” threshold in beta, not “halt canary” by default

Jonas Weber: what about our internal prompt packs (golden prompts) for common tasks? can we reuse those?

Olivia Grant: we can, but they’re not representative of prod prompts for many customers, and they contain a bunch of long-context cases that shadow sampling might under-represent. plus they require storing prompt content to debug (security will push back)

Logan Wright: yeah, security stance is to keep payload storage minimal, esp for shadow outputs. we can store redacted + short-lived samples, but not build the whole eval system around inspecting raw prompts

Selene Huang: another issue: “benchmark prompt sets” aren’t being used in shadow directly anyway. shadow is mirroring real traffic. what we’re really asking is: does judge preference computed on mirrored traffic correlate w/ offline benchmark deltas? answer: sometimes, but not enough to justify shipping “benchmark correlation” as a product promise

Jin Woo Park: +1. operationally we should make sure minimal rubric works across:
- chat
- completions
- tool calls
- json mode

Jonas Weber: ok so decision: minimal judge rubric first, small allowlist `judge_profile=v1_minimal`, plus deterministic checks. and we document that “offline benchmarks are complementary, not gating.”

Selene Huang: yes. and for beta we can add a note: if customers want task-specific scoring, we can configure *one* custom profile per account behind support (no UI), but we don’t want it in mainline yet

Marissa Cole: works. can we capture this in the PRD / guidelines doc so Console copy is aligned?

Olivia Grant: i’ll update the judge scoring guidelines doc w/ the v1 minimal rubric + cautions about gating. also add “known failure modes” section (judge flips on style, verbosity bias, etc.)

Sana Farid: i’ll add stats guidance: minimum sample size before interpreting win-rate, recommend Wilson CI / not raw percent. otherwise people will overreact to noise

Linear Bot: ENG-2448 updated by Olivia Grant — “Eval-harness integration: add LLM-as-judge scorer module and configuration model for shadow runs.”

Jonas Weber: action items:
- Olivia: update guidelines w/ `judge_profile=v1_minimal` + prompt template + failure modes
- Sana: add sample size / CI guidance + suggested default thresholds (warn vs halt)
- Jonas: sync w/ Paula/Marissa on what we surface as beta metrics in Console

Logan Wright: and i’ll ping Thomas Baird / Allison Grant that we’re keeping `judge_profile` as the only judge dimension, no prompt-set tag. :thumbsup:

Selene Huang: :thumbsup: also want to make sure “format adherence” is computed deterministically where possible (schema validation) and judge only used as fallback. reduces cost + noise

Jin Woo Park: +1. if we can emit `shadow_eval.format_valid=true/false` without judge, that’s ideal for rollouts gates

Jonas Weber: cool. closing loop: we ship minimal rubric first. future work: evaluate correlation w/ offline harness later, but not blocking beta

Sana Farid: +1 (and please don’t call it “accuracy” anywhere 😅)

Marissa Cole: noted. copy will be “quality signals” / “preference” not “accuracy”.

Olivia Grant: i’ll post draft in #eng-ml once i push it
